texts: good. "the Keepers" takes its stable name symbol, the habitual present correctly carries no tense, and "during the day" lands on a plain time atom with nothing lost.

bad: two things go wrong — the village is recorded as undergoing the rising rather than doing it, and "late", which is the whole point of the sentence, has no slot anywhere in the instruction set and simply vanishes, leaving the near-empty claim that the village rises. Name the people and state the time instead: "The villagers wake at mid-morning." That also removes the place-standing-for-its-people reading, which the instruction set has no rule for.
good. the state is reified so it can carry the time modifier, the plain "the square is quiet" atom is kept beside it, and "before noon" lands on a proper upper bound.
good. the definite plural becomes a group plus a rule giving each villager their own meal, and "long" stays a plain description of the meal rather than being fused into what the meal is called.

mixed: the parse is faithful, but because the sentence opens with "The Keepers" the determiner is swallowed into the name — here the referent is the_keepers / "The Keepers", while mid-sentence (as in "The Keepers sleep during the day") it is keepers / "Keepers", so the two sentences do not join up. Keep the label off the front of the sentence: "At sundown, before the shift, the Keepers eat a small meal." Worth knowing too that a capitalized plural label is stored as a bare name with no members and no keeper typing, so nothing connects it to the per-Keeper rule in "Each Keeper carries the leather case…".
good. "each Keeper" becomes a rule giving every keeper their own carrying event, the shared case and station stay single referents, and the rule is fireable as written.
good. the companion is recorded as a co-participant rather than a means, the station as the destination, and "senior Keeper" carries both its keeper genus and the senior property.
